claims.text: Rapid quenching of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 produces a predominantly amorphous structure.
The rapidly quenched alloy retains internal stresses and residual heterogeneities.
An isothermal hold near 0.9 times the DSC crystallization-onset temperature constitutes a suitable sub-Tg treatment.
The post-quench hold will promote atomic-level relaxation in the amorphous structure.
The hold will homogenize the amorphous network and reduce internal stress.
Stress relaxation and homogenization will minimize nucleation sites for crystalline phases.
A properly selected hold permits minor atomic rearrangements without supplying enough energy for crystallization.
The relaxation induced by the hold will kinetically hinder primary-phase nucleation and growth during subsequent reheating.
Compared with an untreated control, annealed samples will retain a larger amorphous fraction.
Compared with an untreated control, annealed samples will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature.
The treatment will reduce or delay exothermic crystallization events during reheating.
Rapidly quenched Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits extensive primary crystallization and a complex multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
Holding too briefly or at too low a temperature may fail to produce sufficient relaxation.
Holding too long or at too high a temperature may initiate crystallization or nucleation.
The optimum hold temperature and duration depend on a trade-off between structural relaxation and unintended nucleation.
